title: D-Link DIR-600L end-of-life router has critical unauthenticated stack overflow with public proof of concept
place: Madrid, Spain (INCIBE-CERT, publisher of the advisory)
geo_basis: advisory publisher; the flaw affects devices worldwide
summary: INCIBE-CERT rates CVE-2026-129354 critical (importance 5). In the D-Link DIR-600L router, hardware revision B, firmware 2.17b02, the hnap_main function does not check the length of the HTTP SOAPAction header, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can overflow a stack buffer. A published proof of concept crashes the CGI process in an emulated setup. INCIBE lists exploitation as not observed. D-Link says revision B is end of life.
plain: An old D-Link router that no longer gets updates has a serious flaw that lets anyone on the internet crash it, and a public demonstration exists.
exec: Unsupported edge routers cannot be patched and are easy targets once a public proof of concept exists.
action: Replace DIR-600L rev B routers with a supported model; until then disable remote administration and limit the management interface to a trusted network.
impact: Remote buffer overflow without authentication on an unsupported router; no fix will be issued.
